goal: Create an illustrated Launchpad judging advert for the current TaskGoblin prototype without recorded product footage.
prompt: Create a polished illustrated product advert for TaskGoblin, a Telegram-native AI project manager. Begin with useful commitments disappearing inside a noisy group chat. Show TaskGoblin turning permitted messages into source-linked, reviewable project events using known members, current tasks, recent context and likely-duplicate checks. Show compact Telegram-native UI instead of command-heavy paragraphs: a project home menu, task cards, Confirm/Edit/Ignore controls, owner and deadline selectors, and actionable reminders with Done, Snooze and Change Deadline. Make the trust boundary obvious: model-generated text never directly mutates project state, and consequential inferred changes wait for human confirmation. Show the quiet explicit-completion workflow clearly: the original member message receives a Telegram-supported celebration reaction, its matched task moves to Done, ownership transfers to the member who completed it, and TaskGoblin sends no extra acknowledgement bubble. Show /undo reversing a mistaken task change. Show PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD project context, multi-task proposal batches, private reminders, and the daily 8pm Singapore project report. Finish on the Telegram-authenticated dark web dashboard with list, Kanban and calendar views. Use only implemented commands: /start, /help, /summary, /project, /kpi, /tasks, /mytasks and /undo. Do not show /recent, /addtask, /done, /update, /setproject or /addmilestone. Do not portray TaskGoblin as an autonomous coding agent or claim historical chat access, OCR, WhatsApp support, or silent consequential AI mutation. Use an evidence-led hackathon tone: focused, intelligent, trustworthy and lightly playful. End with 'Turn conversation into accountable project memory' and 'taskgoblin.vercel.app'.

narration.script: Project work already happens in chat. Someone accepts a task, a deadline changes, a blocker appears, and moments later the commitment is buried. TaskGoblin turns permitted Telegram conversations into persistent project memory. It detects proposals, assignments, progress, completions, deadlines, blockers and decisions using known members, current tasks, recent context and project documents. Consequential AI suggestions become reviewable cards, never silent database changes. The team can confirm, ignore, or edit a title, owner or deadline without leaving Telegram. Task cards make the next action obvious: complete, reopen, reassign, reschedule or snooze. Explicit completion stays quiet. When a confidently matched task is finished, TaskGoblin reacts to the original message with a celebration, moves the task to Done and records the person who completed it, without adding another chat bubble. If a task change was wrong, slash undo restores the previous state. Documents can provide bounded context, and one planning request can produce several reviewable tasks. Private reminders offer one-tap actions, while a daily eight PM report highlights progress, urgent work, ownership, blockers and the next seven days. Confirmed state is also available through Telegram login on an editable list, Kanban board and calendar. TaskGoblin keeps humans in control while turning conversation into accountable project memory.

scenes.visuals: A busy illustrated Telegram group pushes 'I will build the API' and 'Due Friday' upward beneath jokes and acknowledgements.
onScreenText: PROJECT WORK ALREADY HAPPENS IN CHAT
scenes.transition: An acid-lime thread catches one disappearing commitment.

scenes.visuals: The source message flows past four compact checks labelled Known Members, Current Tasks, Recent Context and Duplicates, then becomes a source-linked event card.
scenes.transition: The card stops at a visible human-review gate.

scenes.visuals: A compact candidate card explains why a task was detected. Confirm, Edit and Ignore appear. Edit expands progressively into Title, Owner and Deadline, followed by member and date preset buttons.
scenes.transition: The confirmed card clicks into the project timeline.

scenes.visuals: A member writes 'I completed the webhook'. A celebration reaction appears on that exact message. No TaskGoblin reply bubble appears. Beside it, the matched card moves to Done and its owner changes to the completing member. A later /undo briefly restores a mistaken change.
onScreenText: UPDATE THE TASK, NOT THE CHAT NOISE
scenes.transition: The checked task joins a persistent project-memory stack.

scenes.purpose: Show bounded document context and multi-task batches.
scenes.visuals: PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD pages feed a bounded context panel. One planning request fans into several separate reviewable task cards.
onScreenText: PROJECT CONTEXT, NOT JUST ONE MESSAGE
scenes.transition: The cards collapse into a Telegram project home menu.

scenes.visuals: Animate Open Tasks, Due Today, Calendar and Settings. Open one task card with Complete, Owner and Deadline. Then show a private reminder with Done, Snooze and Change Deadline, followed by the daily 8pm project report.
scenes.transition: The dashboard button expands into the web application.

scenes.purpose: Show the secondary web surface and engineering credibility.
scenes.visuals: A dark Telegram-authenticated dashboard moves a task across Kanban, edits its owner and deadline, then switches to Calendar. A brief architecture strip shows verified webhook, deterministic routing, OpenAI Structured Outputs, persisted candidates, Supabase and human confirmation, backed by a test grid.
onScreenText: TELEGRAM FIRST. WEB WHEN YOU NEED IT.
scenes.transition: The system collapses into the TaskGoblin mark.

scenes.purpose: Deliver the promise and call to action.
scenes.visuals: The TaskGoblin logo sits on the dark green canvas with a restrained acid-lime glow. One chat bubble transforms into a checked task card.
onScreenText: TURN CONVERSATION INTO ACCOUNTABLE PROJECT MEMORY
scenes.transition: Hold the final card for two seconds.
